scope: Revision05 only q011 prior-action wording correction and q012 new observation question. Earlier revisions immutable.

before.prompt: Suppose Gold 1 follows your lateral move. What deserves another look?

options.text: The original shot as though Gold 1 had stayed still
A shot without checking the blocker
A pass to D2 or another change of angle

before.explanation: A moving defender can close the new lane, so alternatives remain relevant.

after.prompt: YOU are weighing the two teammate passes. Which direct passing line stays farther from Gold 1 in this view?

options.text: The pass from YOU to D2
The pass from YOU to F1

after.explanation: The line to D2 stays farther from Gold 1 than the line to F1. That makes D2 an option to assess around the current blocker. F1 is farther toward the net and may offer a useful attacking option if that lane remains available. More distance from one defender does not guarantee reception or make D2 the best play in every situation.

optionReasons.reason: D2 is a real teammate. The direct puck-to-D2 segment stays farther from Gold1 than the puck-to-F1 segment. D2 may change the angle but a completed pass/next shot is unproven.

F1 is a real advanced teammate. Its direct segment has less separation from Gold1 but still several metres of point separation; do not call it blocked or wrong generally. It offers a different attacking tradeoff.

geometry.method: Canonical makeScene rendered puck, player receiving centres, finite direct-pass segments and Euclidean point-to-segment minimum distances. No player motion or pass simulated.

duplicateAudit.distinction: q7 identifies D2 against an opponent/goalie; new q5 compares D2 with actual advanced teammate F1, preserves F1’s conditional value and measures the direct lines.

limits: Two genuine same-category choices used; no third real receiving option exists in these selected-player scenes. Chance success is 50%; response is not mastery proof.
Static point geometry does not encode stick reach, body width, skating, passing speed, gaze, interceptions or receiver readiness.
No scene setup or actor moved; no hypothetical event presented as visible.
Q003 phrasing room around line means spacing to the shown gold skaters, not obstruction by every rink feature. Neither compared segment intersects a net or boards.
No rendered/mobile check by author. Exact candidate needs independent content and visual checks.
Author remains advisory-only; no human approval, no source application.
changes.sourceScope: Existing scene sources retained for topic provenance only; no claim they certify these exact comparisons.
changes.revisionReason: Removed unstated prior shot implication; all other after payload fields identical to revision04.

before.prompt: If Gold 2 moves into your new route, what could you do?

options.text: Follow the route without looking
Change direction or stay as another support option
Insist on the return pass anyway

before.explanation: The pass does not obligate the receiver to return it; another support action may be better.

after.prompt: Before offering an inside option, which description matches the two gold defenders in this view?

options.text: Gold 1 is closer to F2; Gold 2 is farther toward the attacking net and nearer the middle
Gold 2 is closer to F2; Gold 1 is farther toward the attacking net and nearer the middle

after.explanation: Gold 1 is close to F2, while Gold 2 is farther toward Gold’s net and nearer the middle across the rink. Account for both the opponent near the carrier and the opponent in the inside space ahead of YOU. Their positions do not prove who will move, which line will stay available or whether F2 will return the puck.

changes.revisionReason: Replaces unnecessary retreat with observation of the two actual defender relationships. No route or prior movement invented.

optionReasons.reason: Gold1 is closer to F2, Gold2 has greater attacking x and smaller |y|; all three comparisons agree with this frame. These are spatial cues, not claimed defensive assignments.
Reverses all three observed comparisons. Both named players are actual opponents, and this arrangement could exist elsewhere, but is not the shown setup.

geometry.method: Euclidean actor distances for stated player relationships; x advances toward attacked right net; |y| measures distance from middle across rink width. makeScene confirms current puck, though this question does not compare puck lanes.

duplicateAudit.distinction: q1 identifies F2 possession; q8 mentions Gold1 facing F2. This question compares Gold1/Gold2 locations, including Gold2 inside/up-ice position; it does not repeat possession, prescribe q4/q9 movement, or ask generic reoffer effectiveness from q6/q10.

limits: Advisory author; no independent/human approval claimed.
Only two matched spatial accounts; random chance 50%, not mastery evidence.
No actual movement, attention, intended marking assignment, reach, timing or successful pass inferred.
No setup edits. No rendered/mobile check by author.
Spatial reading is introductory; challenge and instructional usefulness require independent review.
changes.imageDependency: Prompt and options do not announce which defender occupies each location; player labels and relative positions must be resolved from scene. Briefing provides partial context but does not fully supply Gold2 comparisons.

scenarios.title: The point shot has a blocker
scenarios.objective: Compare the current shooting lane with another angle.
scenarios.briefing: YOU have the puck high in the zone. Gold 1 is directly between YOU and the net. D2 offers a lateral option while F1 is near the far side. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: Gold 1 shares the centre lane between the puck and the attacking net.
YOU have the puck high in the zone. Gold 1 is directly between YOU and the net. D2 offers a lateral option while F1 is near the far side.

questions.prompt: Who stands on the straight line from YOU toward the net?

options.text: F1
Gold 1
D2

questions.explanation: Gold 1 shares the centre lane between the puck and the attacking net.

questions.prompt: Choose two ways to investigate a different shooting opportunity.

options.text: Look for a lateral angle
Assume the puck must go through Gold 1
Check whether D2 has a usable connection

questions.explanation: Moving or passing may change the lane; this picture alone does not prove a shot will reach the net.

questions.prompt: Order one response to the blocked point lane.

options.text: Notice Gold 1 in the lane
Check movement and passing options
Use the option that remains available

questions.explanation: A player may choose a pass, carry or shot depending on the next cue.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a lateral shooting angle.
questions.explanation: A small lateral change shifts the line to the net. Check whether Gold 1 can follow before treating it as open.

questions.prompt: YOU are weighing the two teammate passes. Which direct passing line stays farther from Gold 1 in this view?

options.text: The pass from YOU to D2
The pass from YOU to F1

questions.explanation: The line to D2 stays farther from Gold 1 than the line to F1. That makes D2 an option to assess around the current blocker. F1 is farther toward the net and may offer a useful attacking option if that lane remains available. More distance from one defender does not guarantee reception or make D2 the best play in every situation.

questions.prompt: Why does “move sideways” not guarantee a clear shot?
questions.explanation: Explain that the blocker, other players and goalie can also adjust.

questions.prompt: Which teammate can give YOU a lateral puck option if Gold 1 stays in the shooting line?

options.text: D2
Gold 1
The goalie

questions.explanation: D2 is a Navy teammate at a different lateral angle. Check the route and receiver before passing; Gold 1 may adjust.

questions.prompt: Which two changes could alter the shooting picture?

options.text: D2 moves laterally
YOU change the puck’s angle to the net
Shoot without checking the blocker

questions.explanation: Moving the carrier or finding a lateral pass can change the shooting line. Recheck the blocker and goalie before choosing.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare another puck angle toward the net.
questions.explanation: YOU carry the puck to the example point. It shifts the shooting line slightly and moves closer to Gold 1; neither a clear shot nor a pass to D2 is guaranteed.

questions.prompt: Why does a blocker make the read about geometry rather than simply shooting harder?
questions.explanation: Gold 1 occupies the direct line, so angle, screen and support determine what is visible; if those do not change, more force does not create a lane.

scenarios.title: Offer again after a short pass
scenarios.objective: Recognize a useful off-puck movement after passing.
scenarios.briefing: YOU have just passed to F2. Gold 1 faces F2 near the boards. You are still in the place from which you passed; the exercise asks you to seek another visible option. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: The puck is now assigned to F2 after the stated pass.
YOU have just passed to F2. Gold 1 faces F2 near the boards. You are still in the place from which you passed; the exercise asks you to seek another visible option.

questions.prompt: Which player is the new puck carrier?

options.text: F2
YOU
Gold 2

questions.explanation: The puck is now assigned to F2 after the stated pass.

questions.prompt: Which two reads help before reoffering?

options.text: Whether the return pass is guaranteed
The space available beyond your old spot
The defender’s attention and position

questions.explanation: A give-and-go needs a real route and a prepared carrier, not just a memorized pattern.

questions.prompt: Arrange one reoffer routine.

options.text: Confirm the pass arrived
Scan the next support space
Move and become visible again

questions.explanation: The route should change if the defenders remove the expected opening.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to illustrate a new inside option for F2.
questions.explanation: Moving into different ice changes the passing picture. The reference is only useful if Gold 2 and Gold 1 cannot remove that route.

questions.prompt: Before offering an inside option, which description matches the two gold defenders in this view?

options.text: Gold 1 is closer to F2; Gold 2 is farther toward the attacking net and nearer the middle
Gold 2 is closer to F2; Gold 1 is farther toward the attacking net and nearer the middle

questions.explanation: Gold 1 is close to F2, while Gold 2 is farther toward Gold’s net and nearer the middle across the rink. Account for both the opponent near the carrier and the opponent in the inside space ahead of YOU. Their positions do not prove who will move, which line will stay available or whether F2 will return the puck.

questions.prompt: How can you judge whether your second movement improved the play?
questions.explanation: Look for a new useful route, space created for F2 or a defender moved—not only whether you received a return pass.

questions.prompt: What can YOU call to make F2 aware of your reoffer?

options.text: Inside option when you can see me
The first pass is still coming
No need to look at pressure

questions.explanation: The call names a new inside option while leaving F2 to confirm the lane; if Gold 1 tracks the route, re-space before asking for the puck.

questions.prompt: Which two cues should drive your second movement?

options.text: F2’s new puck position
Gold 1 facing F2
Your original spot staying fixed

questions.explanation: The new carrier location and defender orientation shape the return lane; staying fixed can leave you behind pressure.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare another passing angle for F2.
questions.explanation: The example changes the passing angle. It is farther from F2 than the starting spot, so it is not automatically a shorter release. Recheck both defenders before calling for a pass.

questions.prompt: How can YOU tell a reoffer is helping instead of just following the puck?
questions.explanation: It should change the passing angle and preserve separation from Gold 1, while keeping another teammate useful; if it closes every lane, re-space.
